The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1518c8e1e86bb532), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: For every finite m ≥ 10, finite jet budget N, positive loss tolerance ηout, and 0 < ν < 1, one can choose ζ > 0 and finite construction orders so that the following objects exist for arbitrarily large T along the indicated sequence. 1. There are exact smooth complete vacuum data dT ∈ D on the whole bridge with pm(dT −d) → 0. They agree with d on the other end, the connecting region, and an expanding protected ball on the selected end. The permitted exterior correction tail is retained. 2. An exact exterior evolution of dT reaches the required part of S, with overlapping collars and strict outflow margins. In the fixed background wave-map description its entry spacetime jets differ from g + hp by O(A2 T eηoutT ). Here hp = AT tr. rev.g Re  eiλv J∗ X j=0 λ−j pj   . (4.3) The leading coefficient is real, trace-free, and annihilates L0. On the entire observation box QT , |(p0)AB|γ ≥ e−o(T) . (4.4) At every fixed required base order the ordinary mixed coordinate jets of the normalized amplitude components are eo(T), and the linearized Ricci and gauge errors have arbitrarily high inverse- frequency accuracy. 3. There is a metric ḡ exactly of double-null form, with fields γ̄, log Ā, b̄ and their exact geo- metric derived fields. Through order N, its differences from the background fields, including q−1∂vb, are O(AT eηoutT ). Its defects in the null structure and angular equations (5.4)–(5.7) are O(A2 T eηoutT ). If the actual exterior induced data are written in double-null coordinates initialized by the background values on S, their full entry jets differ from this template by the same quadratic bound. All entry discrepancies and all template changes and defects vanish for v < (1 −ν)T. Any additional finite initial or residual jet buffers may be included in N. Positive frequency powers at these base orders are independent of the later orders used to improve linear accuracy. At the finitely many high entry orders ultimately requested by Theorem 5.1, the actual fields have eo(T) bounds.
